issue: Should the UK introduce a universal basic income?
opinions: Yes. A basic income would end poverty, simplify the benefits system and give people security as automation takes jobs.
No, paying everyone money regardless of need is a huge waste. It would cost a fortune and require massive tax rises.
I worry it would make people stop working. There has to be an incentive to contribute to society.
It's worth testing with proper pilot schemes before deciding. The trials so far have been small and short.
A basic income would give carers, artists and volunteers recognition for valuable work that currently goes unpaid.

issue: Should nuclear power be expanded to fight climate change?
opinions: Yes, nuclear is low carbon and provides steady power when the wind isn't blowing and the sun isn't shining. We can't hit net zero without it.
No. Nuclear waste stays dangerous for thousands of years and nobody has a safe place to store it.
New nuclear plants are far too expensive and take decades to build. That money would cut more emissions if spent on renewables and insulation.
I support small modular reactors, which could be cheaper and quicker to build, but not more giant plants like Hinkley Point.
After Fukushima and Chernobyl I simply don't trust it. One accident can make a whole region uninhabitable.

issue: Should junk food advertising be banned?
opinions: Yes, especially adverts aimed at children. Obesity is a crisis and companies spend billions persuading kids to eat sugar.
No. Adults can make their own choices. The government shouldn't decide what we're allowed to see advertised.
Advertising is only part of the problem. Healthy food is too expensive, and people need cooking skills and time.
I'd ban it before the 9pm watershed and online where children are watching, but not completely.
A ban would hurt broadcasters and sports clubs that depend on the advertising money.

issue: Should the monarchy be abolished?
opinions: Yes. In a democracy no one should be head of state just because of who their parents are. We should elect our head of state.
No, the monarchy brings stability and continuity, and the King stays above party politics.
The royal family brings in a lot of tourism and does a huge amount of charity work. It is worth what it costs.
Keep it but slim it down. Fewer royals on the public payroll and more transparency about their finances.
It doesn't really matter to me either way. There are far more important problems like the cost of living, so this debate is a distraction.

issue: Should voting be compulsory?
opinions: Yes, as in Australia. Compulsory voting means governments represent everyone, not just the groups who turn out.
No. Freedom includes the freedom not to vote, and forcing people would just produce random or spoiled ballots.
I'd only support it if there is a 'none of the above' option on the ballot so people can register a protest.
The real problem is that people feel politicians don't listen. Fix that and turnout will rise on its own.
Make voting easier instead, with weekend polling days and online voting, rather than fining people.

issue: Should the state pension age be raised?
opinions: Yes. People live much longer than when pensions were introduced, and the country can't afford to pay pensions for thirty years.
No, it's unfair on manual workers whose bodies wear out. A builder or cleaner can't keep working until 70.
Life expectancy varies hugely between rich and poor areas, so a single pension age punishes people in poorer regions.
It should rise slowly and with plenty of warning so people can plan. Sudden changes have already hurt many women.
Instead of raising the age, make wealthy pensioners contribute more and stop the triple lock rising so fast.

issue: Should rent controls be introduced in big cities?
opinions: Yes. Rents have gone up far faster than wages and people are being forced out of the cities where they work.
No, rent controls reduce the supply of rental homes because landlords sell up, and quality falls. It has failed in many cities.
The only real solution is building far more homes, including council housing. Controls just treat the symptom.
Limit how much rent can increase each year for existing tenants, which protects people without freezing the market.
As a small landlord, my costs have risen with mortgage rates. Controls would make renting out my flat unaffordable.

issue: Should mobile phones be banned in schools?
opinions: Yes, phones are a constant distraction in class and are behind a lot of bullying. Schools that ban them have better results.
No. Parents need to be able to contact their children, especially on the way to and from school.
Phones should be locked away during lessons but students should learn to use technology responsibly rather than having it banned.
It should be left to each head teacher to decide, not imposed nationally.
The bigger problem is social media, not phones. A ban at school won't help if children are online all evening.

issue: Should sugary drinks be taxed more heavily?
opinions: Yes. The sugar tax has already made manufacturers cut sugar, so extending it would help fight obesity and tooth decay.
No, it's a regressive tax that hits poorer families hardest while rich people barely notice.
Taxing drinks is fine, but the money must go into school sports and healthy meals, otherwise it's just a cash grab.
People should be free to choose what they drink. Education works better than punishing people with taxes.
It would make more sense to tax sugar in all processed food, not just drinks, which are only a small part of the problem.

issue: Should cannabis be legalised?
opinions: Yes. Prohibition has failed. Legalising and regulating it would take money away from criminal gangs and raise tax.
No, cannabis can cause psychosis, especially strong skunk used by teenagers. Legalising it sends the message it is safe.
It should be legal for medical use, which helps people with epilepsy and chronic pain, but not for recreation.
Decriminalise possession so people are not given criminal records, but keep selling it illegal.
I've seen what drugs did to my family. Making it easier to get will lead to more people using harder drugs.

issue: Should national service be reintroduced for young people?
opinions: Yes. It would teach discipline, bring together young people from different backgrounds, and give them useful skills.
No. Forcing young people into the military or volunteering is a waste of their time and an infringement of their freedom.
A voluntary scheme with incentives, like help with university fees, would work better than compulsion.
If it happens, it must include community and care work, not just the armed forces.
The cost would be enormous and the money would be better spent on youth services that were cut.

issue: Should private schools lose their tax advantages?
opinions: Yes. Private schools are businesses for the wealthy, not charities, and taxpayers shouldn't subsidise them.
No. Parents who pay fees also pay taxes for state schools they don't use, saving the state money.
Taxing them will push some smaller schools to close and send thousands of children into already crowded state schools.
They should keep the tax relief only if they share facilities and offer many more free places to local children.
The focus should be on raising standards in state schools so that nobody feels they need to go private.

issue: Should genetically modified crops be allowed?
opinions: Yes, GM crops can resist pests and drought, reduce pesticide use and help feed a growing population.
No. We don't know the long-term effects on health and the environment, and the risks are irreversible once released.
My concern is big corporations patenting seeds and making farmers dependent on them.
Allow them but with strict testing and clear labelling so consumers can choose.
Gene editing that only speeds up natural breeding is fine, but inserting genes from other species goes too far.

issue: Should there be a cap on immigration?
opinions: Yes. Public services, housing and the NHS can't keep up with the numbers arriving every year.
No. Immigrants fill vital jobs in care, health and farming. A cap would cause shortages and damage the economy.
Immigration should be based on skills the country needs, with a points system rather than a fixed number.
We have a moral duty to take refugees fleeing war and persecution, and they should not count towards any cap.
The debate is too heated. We need honest figures and a system that is fair and properly enforced.

issue: Should assisted dying be legalised?
opinions: Yes. Terminally ill people who are suffering should have the right to choose a peaceful death.
No. Vulnerable and elderly people could feel pressure to end their lives so they are not a burden on their families.
Better palliative care is the answer. If people had good end-of-life care, few would ask to die.
Allow it only for terminally ill adults with six months to live, with approval from two doctors and a judge.
As a person of faith, I believe life is sacred and it is not for us to decide when it ends.

issue: Should public transport be free?
opinions: Yes, free buses and trains would get people out of cars, cut pollution and help people on low incomes get to work.
No. Someone still has to pay, and the money would be better spent on making services more frequent and reliable.
It should be free for young people, students and the elderly, but everyone else should pay something.
In rural areas there are hardly any buses at all. Free fares are pointless if there's no service.
Free transport might lead to overcrowding and antisocial behaviour on services that are already packed.

issue: Should the BBC licence fee be scrapped?
opinions: Yes. It's unfair to force people to pay for the BBC when they watch streaming services instead. It should move to subscriptions.
No. The licence fee keeps the BBC independent from government and advertisers and pays for quality programmes for everyone.
Replace it with funding from general taxation, scaled to income, so poorer households pay less.
I'm fed up with BBC bias and huge salaries for presenters. Why should I pay for that?
The BBC World Service and local radio are vital public services that commercial broadcasters would never provide.

issue: Should children be allowed to use AI tools for homework?
opinions: Yes. AI is part of the world they're growing up in, and learning to use it well is an essential skill.
No. If AI writes their essays, children never learn to think, write or solve problems for themselves.
AI can be a great tutor that explains things step by step, as long as teachers set tasks that can't simply be copied.
It widens inequality: children with paid AI subscriptions and tech-savvy parents get ahead.
Schools need clear rules and to teach children about AI making mistakes and inventing facts.

issue: Should the government limit how many flights people can take?
opinions: Yes. Aviation is one of the fastest-growing sources of emissions, and a small number of frequent flyers cause most of them.
No, that's a huge intrusion into personal freedom. People have the right to travel and see family abroad.
A frequent flyer levy that increases with each flight would be fairer than a hard limit.
Invest in high-speed rail and ban short domestic flights where trains are a real alternative.
Ordinary families taking one holiday a year are not the problem. Target private jets and business travel first.

issue: Should animal testing for medicines be banned?
opinions: Yes. It causes huge suffering and animals are often poor models for humans, so many drugs that pass animal tests still fail.
No. Animal testing is still necessary to make sure new medicines are safe before they're given to people.
It should be phased out as alternatives like organ-on-a-chip and computer models improve, with funding to speed them up.
Testing should be allowed only for serious diseases, never for cosmetics or minor products, and with strict welfare rules.
As someone with a chronic illness, I depend on medicines that were tested on animals. Banning it would cost human lives.
